rules_evaluated.evidence: Doc (M6-in-detail, permission-beat paragraph): 'Plain stats from the generation session ... then the concrete things that went sideways, then the generalisation (everyone struggles; surprises happen; the LLM is not a deterministic machine), then a short beat on what the trainer did with the misses ..., then the landing that hands the loop to the student. Permission-giving, not credibility-performance, and it reads best once the student has just run the loop themselves.' File structure matches beat-for-beat: L7-11 (## The numbers, plain stats), L13-27 (## Things that went sideways), L29-39 (## The generalisation — L31/33/35 quote the doc's three sentences verbatim), L41-45 (## Then I compounded the session — what the trainer did with the misses), L47-59 (## What the loop is for — the handoff: 'Your job is not to stop the drift. Your job is to catch it and encode what you learned.' L53; 'Your turn.' L57). Emotional exit: normalized struggle / permission, not shame — sets up the Human close (personal-reflection round) and the training's own close by handing the loop to the student rather than resolving the tension for them (L51: 'A rule you wrote last module will not apply this session. That is the thing... every session surprises you, even when the task looked the same.' stays open, does not pre-resolve). Closest-to-violating line checked: L45 'The model is good. It is still not 100% deterministic.' — reads as a tidy aphoristic close mid-lecture; stays inside because it sits before the final beat (## What the loop is for), which reopens rather than seals the tension ('The loop exists because LLMs drift... your job is not to stop the drift'), so the mood is not resolved-too-early at the point that would steal the module's own close. This diff since the prior instance (git diff 9a6d906e..HEAD) also tightened 'the next hour you will diagnose gaps' to 'You have just diagnosed gaps' (L49) — a fix toward the doc's own note that this beat lands after the exercises, not before, strengthening rather than weakening this rule's fit.

Failures throughout are narrated as factual session events attributed to the model or the process, not as shame directed at a present person. Closest-to-violating line checked: L21 'That is a Claude-miss, not a rule-leak. The rule was right. Claude did not apply it.' — assigns the miss explicitly to Claude (the agent, absent from the room) in diagnostic language ('a Claude-miss'), not punitive language aimed at the student; stays inside because the very next clause reframes it as a limitation of the tool ('The rule was right') rather than a moral failing. The lecture's own closing register is not-knowing throughout: L31/33/35 name a condition ('Everyone struggles. Surprises happen. The LLM is not a deterministic machine.'), L45 'The model is good. It is still not 100% deterministic.', L53 'Your job is not to stop the drift. Your job is to catch it and encode what you learned.' No line addresses the student as having done wrong; the narrator's own self-directed lines (L9 'Five taste reversals from me on Claude's confident recommendations'; L27's account of missing a verbatim check) are course-correction reporting, not confession.

The file's own maintainer block carries the explicit control for this rule (L87, 'Design constraint (session turn 8)'): 'the Story names the CONDITION (non-determinism, universal struggle) without restating the SPECIFIC failure modes the student meets in the two-session diff. Meta-failure (curriculum generation drifting, banned-word leak, rules loaded late) is not student-run failure (packaged run drifts at hour 2, memory thin on the critical file). Same condition, different domain.' Confirmed against body: none of the seven catalogued failure modes (chat-shaped opening, banned word, flattering end-state, unrun sims, self-contradicting closer, shipped paraphrase, uncited frame) describes what the student's own packaged run will specifically do wrong — they are all about the M6 curriculum-generation session, a different domain from the M6 exercise's diagnosis task. Checked the one term that could front-run a naming moment — 'eval': the strategy doc states 'M6 is where the word [eval] earns its full weight, directly after the exercise debrief' and per the module file's own deck order ('the-2-frontiers → exercise spot-gaps-build-the-loop → composing-the-workflow [control loop, Eval, cadence...] → exercise read-your-stack → the-handoff-prompt → story-of-module-6 → Human close → agents-that-build-agents'), composing-the-workflow.md names/teaches 'Eval' well before story-of-module-6 runs — so this lecture's passing references to 'the sims and evals' (L21, backing L84/98) are a callback to an already-taught term, not a front-run of it. Also checked the doc's own note that 'No M6 slide carries either company — but story-of-module-6.md names Ramp in body ... That is the memo owning its own mistake, not an anchor case' — confirmed the Ramp/Charles paragraph (L25) is framed exactly that way (the trainer's own misquote), not as a teaching anchor-case that would duplicate the anchor-case material that lives elsewhere.
